summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Earth's history is divided into Eons, Eras, Periods, and Epochs. Precambrian Eon saw the origin of cellular life (~2.0 bya). Paleozoic Era: Age of Invertebrates & Fishes (Devonian). Mesozoic Era: Age of Reptiles (Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous) ending with dinosaur extinction ~65 mya. Cenozoic Era: Age of Mammals and Angiosperms.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Major Geological Eras & Evolutionary Milestones
1. **Precambrian Eon** (4.5 bya – 541 mya):
   - Origin of non-cellular life ($\approx 3.0\text{ bya}$) and first cellular forms ($\approx 2.0\text{ bya}$).
   - Emergence of oxygenic photosynthesis (cyanobacteria) transforming the atmosphere from reducing to oxidizing.
2. **Paleozoic Era** (541 – 252 mya):
   - Cambrian Explosion: Invertebrate phyla diversified.
   - **Devonian Period**: "Age of Fishes"; first amphibians invaded land.
   - **Carboniferous Period**: Coal-forming giant ferns and lycopods; "Age of Amphibians".
3. **Mesozoic Era** (252 – 66 mya) — "Age of Reptiles & Gymnosperms":
   - **Triassic**: Origin of first dinosaurs and egg-laying mammals.
   - **Jurassic**: Dominance of giant dinosaurs; emergence of *Archaeopteryx*.
   - **Cretaceous**: Radiation of flowering plants (angiosperms); abrupt mass extinction of dinosaurs $\approx 65\text{ million years ago}$ (K-Pg boundary bolide impact).
4. **Cenozoic Era** (66 mya – Present) — "Age of Mammals & Angiosperms":
   - Adaptive radiation of placental mammals, birds, and angiosperms.
   - Quaternary Period: Emergence of hominids and modern humans.

### 9.2 Coelacanth (*Latimeria*)
- A lobe-finned fish caught in South Africa (1938), previously thought to have gone extinct $65\text{ mya}$.
- Serves as a **"Living Fossil"** and transitional form demonstrating how fleshy, paired fins evolved into the tetrapod limbs of amphibians.

conceptBreakdown.heading: The Five Mass Extinction Events
conceptBreakdown.title: The Five Mass Extinction Events
conceptBreakdown.content: Earth has experienced 5 major mass extinction pulses (Big Five): End-Ordovician, Late-Devonian, End-Permian ('The Great Dying' - 95% marine species lost), End-Triassic, and End-Cretaceous (dinosaur extinction ~65 mya).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Fossil Dating: Carbon-14 and Uranium-Lead
conceptBreakdown.title: Fossil Dating: Carbon-14 and Uranium-Lead
conceptBreakdown.content: Radiometric dating uses radioisotope decay: Carbon-14 dating (half-life 5,730 years) for recent organic fossils up to 50,000 years, and Uranium-Lead / Potassium-Argon dating for older geological rock strata spanning millions of years.
